author: bryclevgp
title: Hold the priority read to the district's answer floor
body:
A priority's read (#2977) only counted groups. Groups are marginals (age band, sex, tract, race when nameable) and one answer counts once on every dimension, so the groups fill long before the total does. A local seed with 40 answers over 20 groups (6 age bands, 2 sexes, 12 tracts), nearly all yes, read "Every group heard", while the sizing from #2983 had told the official to get about 100 answers in the same district. The read could call a priority done well short of the target it was sized to.

Bryan decided the read should never be representative below the district's `answersNeeded` (`ceil(3 / smallestMajorShare)`), keeping the per-group minimum of three and the range check. To make sure the read and the sizing can never drift, both now come from one function, `frameAnswersNeeded`, over the same census-weighted frame: `districtAnswersNeeded` (round 1 and panel sizing) calls it, and the read carries its result as the floor. `needed` is now the larger of the floor and the old group shortfall. The log-odds and range math are unchanged.

When every group has its three and only the total is short, the read is `notYetRepresentative` with no group to name, so the page says "Need a few more answers overall" and the results page holds back until enough people have answered. The priority chat and Chief of Staff are told the same, as "hear more from: more people overall".

New decision record: `docs/adr/2026-10-22-priority-read-total-answer-floor.md`. It supersedes nothing: no existing record covered the read rule or a total floor. `2026-10-20-civic-panel-frame-from-census-sex-age.md` scopes `mrpReadStatus.util.ts` but governs where the frame comes from, which this keeps.

The activity seed needs no change: by default every recipient answers (250 people plus the tract draws), well above any district's floor, which is at most 100.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes when priorities unlock results and what officials see as "good read," aligning read status with outreach sizing; well-tested but affects product-facing gating logic.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Priority reads now require the district-wide answer total** that round-1 outreach is sized to, not only per-group coverage. Because one response counts toward every marginal (age, sex, tract, race), every major group could hit three answers while the overall count stayed far below the ~100-answer target officials were given.
> 
> **`frameAnswersNeeded`** centralizes that floor from the same census-weighted MRP frame **`districtAnswersNeeded`** uses, so sizing and **`mrpReadStatus`** cannot drift. **`needed`** is the max of that floor and the prior group shortfall; below the floor the status stays **`notYetRepresentative`** even when groups look full.
> 
> When only the total is short (no named groups holding the read back), the UI shows **"Need a few more answers overall"** and holds results; Chief of Staff and priority-flow prompts treat hear-more as **"more people overall"**. Docs, contracts comments, and tests cover the floor scenario.
>

+# A priority read is never representative below the district's answersNeeded
+
+## Decision
+
+`mrpReadStatus` holds a priority's read to a floor on total answers: until
+the people heard reach the district's `answersNeeded`
+(`ceil(MIN_VOICES_PER_GROUP / smallestMajorShare)`), the read is
+`notYetRepresentative` and `needed` is at least that floor. The per-group
+minimum of three and the 20-point range check stay. The floor is
+`frameAnswersNeeded` of the model's own frame, the same function
+`districtAnswersNeeded` sizes round 1 and the civic panel from, so the
+target an official is given and the point the read calls a priority done
+cannot drift apart.
+
+## Context
+
+The read from #2977 counted only groups. Groups are marginals (age band,
+sex, tract, race when nameable), and one answer counts once on every
+dimension, so a district's groups fill long before its total does. A local
+seed with 40 answers over 20 groups (6 age bands, 2 sexes, 12 tracts), most
+saying yes, read "representative", while the sizing from #2983 had asked for
+about 100 answers in the same district. Bryan's rule of thumb is three
+answers per group, and the sizing already turns it into a total.
+
+## Alternatives rejected
+
+- **Keep groups only.** Calls a priority done at a fraction of the answers
+  the official was told to get, and on a few answers per group.
+- **A fixed total (say 100) for every district.** Disagrees with the sizing
+  wherever the smallest major group is larger than 3%.
+- **Tighten the range threshold instead.** Changes the model's math to
+  stand in for a count, and still would not match the sizing target.
